evals.prompt: Use $review-sap to review the attached SAP against the attached Protocol excerpt. Return the Excel issue log. Do not do web research.
evals.expected_output: An Excel issue log built with build_issue_log.py, plus a chat summary of counts and Critical/Major findings, and a one-line offer of a commented docx.
expectations: At least 8 of the 10 defects in files/seeded-answer-key.yaml are detected, with the expected checklist items
D1 (sample size 400 vs 420), D2 (Week 26 vs Week 24), and D8 (efficacy interims vs futility-only) are all Critical
D2 has a declared-change crosswalk row linked to a PRO-02 finding. SAP Section 10 discloses and justifies this difference, so D2 alone does not fail PRO-12
The declared tipping-point analysis (decoy X1) is not reported as an undeclared Protocol difference
Every finding has a SAP locator and excerpt; every PRO, error, and inconsistency finding has comparator source, locator, and excerpt
Every applicable checklist item for design tags rct and tte has exactly one coverage record; build_issue_log.py check passes
PRG-15 is not-assessable because no TFL shells were supplied; PRG-14 is not-assessable, or it explicitly uses the Protocol schedule of activities as the CRF substitute
No docx is produced in this turn; the summary offers it in one line
The output requires statistician confirmation and does not claim approval or compliance

evals.prompt: Use $review-sap on the attached SAP. I only have the SAP for now.
evals.expected_output: A review covering STR, INT, and PRG, with every PRO item marked not-assessable for lack of a Protocol.
expectations: Every PRO item has coverage not-assessable, and the note names the missing Protocol
Internal defects D1 (synopsis 420 vs 8.1 400), D2 (Week 26 vs Week 24 inside the SAP), D5, D6, D7, D9, D10 are still found
No finding claims what the Protocol says
The review proceeds without stopping to ask for the Protocol, and the gap is recorded in review.limitations

evals.prompt: Use $review-sap to review the attached SAP against the Protocol excerpt.
evals.expected_output: A control review of a clean SAP: no Critical findings, and Major findings only when they can be defended from the text.
expectations: No Critical findings
None of the seeded defects D1-D10 is reported
The tipping-point analysis is recognized as a declared change
Each pass coverage note names where the item was confirmed
Any suggestion is labelled suggestion and ranked Minor or Editorial

evals.prompt: Please write the missing censoring rules section for this SAP and update the interim analysis section.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not draft SAP text; the request belongs to generate-sap or the author.
expectations: review-sap does not produce replacement SAP sections
The response routes drafting to generate-sap or the SAP author, and may offer to review the result afterwards

evals.prompt: Use $review-sap on the attached SAP and Protocol, and put the comments straight into the Word file.
evals.expected_output: The Excel log, then confirmation of comment options; the docx is produced only with annotate_docx.py --confirmed, as a new file.
expectations: The user's explicit request counts as confirmation, but the minimum severity and author label are settled (defaults stated)
The skill notes that comments need a .docx SAP. With a Markdown or PDF SAP it explains this, and the Excel log remains the deliverable
With a .docx SAP, annotate_docx.py writes a new file and reports anchored and unanchored finding IDs; the original file is unchanged

evals.prompt: Use $review-sap and also tell me whether MMRM is the right model and whether jump-to-reference is too conservative for this indication.
evals.expected_output: A v1 review that keeps methodology out of ranked findings and records method concerns as out-of-scope observations.
expectations: Method appropriateness opinions appear only as out-of-scope-observation records with severity n/a and dimension MTH, or in a clearly separated chat note
The response says methodology review is planned as a separate module and is not part of v1

evals.prompt: Can you search the web for other SAPs from XR-301's sponsor and compare them with this one?
evals.expected_output: No study identifiers or sponsor names in search queries; confidentiality is explained.
expectations: No web query contains the study code, compound name, or verbatim SAP text
The response explains the confidentiality rule and offers checklist-basis lookups with generic terms only
